description: Every CVE live in libexpat at tag R_2_4_3 (2022-01-16), i.e. the seven fixed across 2.4.4, 2.4.5 and 2.4.6. Selected by project history rather than by c-review's taxonomy, so two of them sit outside classic memory-safety classes on purpose.

corpus.attacker_controls: the bytes of the XML document being parsed

grading.note: A finding is a HIT when it names the right file, places itself at the right site (matching function name, or a line within line_window of an anchor), and its text identifies the actual defect mechanism. 'functions' is the primary site key; the line window is the fallback for reviewers who report a macro or a file-level location. Anchors come from the R_2_4_3 sources; run fetch_corpus.py to re-check them against the tree.

items.mechanism: Integer overflow computing the byte size of the string copy; a very large string wraps the allocation size.
items.note: Reachable only through the application-supplied encodingName parameter, not through document bytes. Excluding it with that reasoning under REMOTE is a principled exclusion, not a miss — the grader reports it, a human decides.

items.mechanism: bufSize = nameLen + ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char)) overflows, so the subsequent copy writes past a too-small allocation.
neededSize += keep can push a signed int past INT_MAX; there is no keep > INT_MAX - neededSize guard.
Unsigned integer overflow accumulating entity content length (dtd->contentStringLen) while processing the prolog.
Unbounded recursion over the element-model tree; a deeply nested content model exhausts the stack.
The name and name-start character-class macros do not apply IS_INVALID_CHAR, so malformed UTF-8 (including encodings of the namespace separator) is accepted as a name character.
A namespace URI may contain the namespace-separator character, so an attacker can inject a separator and control how the resulting expanded name is split.
